mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT a service provided by an operating system?
o: Translating source code into machine code
mcq.e: Translating source code into machine code is the compiler's job. IPC, resource management and program execution are OS services.

mcq.q: A well-behaved operating system is characterised by which pair of qualities?
o: Low throughput and high turnaround time
High throughput and low turnaround time
High throughput and high turnaround time
Low throughput and low turnaround time
mcq.e: A good OS completes much work per unit time (high throughput) and finishes jobs quickly (low turnaround time).

mcq.q: Which type of operating system marked the beginning of interactive computer communication?
mcq.e: Batch systems ran jobs with no interaction; time-sharing gave each user CPU slices in rotation and made interaction possible.

mcq.q: In a time-sharing system, when a process's time slice expires, its state changes from:
mcq.e: The process was not waiting for I/O, so it goes back to the ready queue (Running to Ready), never to Blocked.

mcq.q: Which statement about distributed operating systems is NOT a benefit?
mcq.e: High communication latency is a cost of distributed systems. Scalability, resource sharing and fault tolerance are benefits.

mcq.q: Which pairing is correct?
o: Parallel processing is loosely coupled; distributed is tightly coupled
Parallel processing is tightly coupled; distributed is loosely coupled
Both parallel and distributed are tightly coupled
Both parallel and distributed are loosely coupled
mcq.e: Parallel processing is tightly coupled, distributed systems are loosely coupled. Exam statements reversing this are false.

mcq.q: A real-time operating system has well-defined fixed time constraints and comes in which two types?
mcq.e: Real-time systems are classified as hard real-time and soft real-time, and typically run on embedded systems.

mcq.q: A system in which more than one process resides in main memory at the same time is called:
mcq.e: Multiprogramming keeps several processes in memory to raise CPU utilisation. Multiprocessing uses two or more CPUs.

mcq.q: Which term describes a system in which two or more CPUs are shared by programs?
mcq.e: Multiprocessing means two or more CPUs. Multithreading is a program broken into smaller parts loaded as needed.

mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT an operating system?
mcq.e: LDAP is a protocol, not an operating system.

mcq.q: Which statement about the kernel is FALSE?
o: It is the innermost layer of the OS
It is always resident in main memory
It is the first part of the OS loaded during booting
It is a collection of separately loadable programs
mcq.e: The kernel is the memory-resident core loaded at boot and stays for the whole session; it is not a set of separately loadable programs.

mcq.q: Which statement comparing mode switch and context switch is correct?
o: A user-kernel mode switch costs less than a process context switch
A user-kernel mode switch costs more than a process context switch
Privileged instructions can run in user mode
mcq.e: In a mode switch the address space does not change, so it is cheaper. Privileged instructions run only in kernel mode.

mcq.q: In a monolithic kernel design, which statement is FALSE?
o: User and kernel services share one address space
User and kernel services run in separate address spaces
mcq.e: A monolithic kernel keeps user and kernel services in ONE address space; the 'separate address space' claim is false.

mcq.q: Which operating system is described as a hybrid kernel (Mach microkernel plus BSD)?
mcq.e: OS X uses the XNU kernel, a combination of the Mach microkernel and BSD components.

mcq.q: A virtual machine is best described as:
o: Abstracting one computer's hardware into several execution environments so multiple OSs run concurrently
A disk area used to store output before printing
A table that maps pages to frames
mcq.e: A virtual machine (managed by a hypervisor) gives several execution environments on one computer. Spooling is the disk-buffered output idea.

mcq.q: A 32-bit operating system can address at most how much RAM?
mcq.e: 2^32 bytes = 4 GB is the address ceiling of a 32-bit OS.

mcq.q: Which Process Control Block field is NOT normally listed as part of a PCB?
mcq.e: A PCB holds process ID, state, program counter, registers, memory limits and open files; a compiler version is not part of it.

mcq.q: During a context switch, which of the following need NOT be saved?
o: PCB contents of the old process
mcq.e: The TLB is flushed rather than saved. Registers and the program counter must be saved in the PCB.

mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT a valid process state?
mcq.e: Valid states are new, ready, running, waiting (blocked) and terminated. 'Excite' is not a state.

mcq.q: Which process state transition is impossible?
mcq.e: The dispatcher picks only from the ready queue, so a blocked process must first become Ready when its I/O completes.

mcq.q: A process that has completed execution but still has an entry in the process table is called a:
mcq.e: A zombie has finished but awaits reaping by its parent. An orphan is a process whose parent died first.

mcq.q: What does fork() return to the child process on success?
mcq.e: fork() returns 0 to the child, the child's PID to the parent, and -1 on failure.

mcq.q: Which Windows function releases a handle to a resource?
mcq.e: CloseHandle takes a handle to the resource; CloseFile() does not exist. Skipping CloseHandle leaks resources.

mcq.q: Which of these is a system-call category?
mcq.e: Categories are process control, file manipulation, device manipulation, information maintenance and communication. 'Data compilation' is not one.

mcq.q: Which statement about a trap is correct?
o: It is software-generated, such as divide-by-zero or a system call
It is a hardware-generated interrupt from a peripheral
It is generated only by the compiler
It is the same as a context switch
mcq.e: A trap is raised by the running instruction (software-generated). Calling it a hardware-generated interrupt is the false claim.

mcq.q: Which resource is NOT shared among threads of the same process?
mcq.e: Each thread has its own stack (user and kernel), along with its own thread ID, program counter and registers.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a genuine benefit of multithreading?
o: Faster execution on a single-core CPU
mcq.e: A single core still runs one thread at a time, so threads give no raw speed-up there.

mcq.q: Which statement about user-level and kernel-level threads is FALSE?
o: User-level threads are faster to create than kernel-level threads
Kernel-level threads are faster to manage than user-level threads
One blocking call can block a whole process with user-level threads
mcq.e: User-level threads need no kernel calls so they are faster; the claim that kernel threads are faster is false.

mcq.q: In asynchronous thread cancellation:
o: The target thread is terminated immediately
Only a flag is set for the target to check
mcq.e: Asynchronous cancellation kills the target at once; deferred cancellation merely sets a flag the target checks.

mcq.q: Which scheduler is responsible for swapping (load control)?
mcq.e: Long-term = job admission, medium-term = swapping, short-term = CPU scheduling.

mcq.q: The time taken by the dispatcher to stop one process and start another is called:
mcq.e: The dispatcher performs the context switch; the time it takes is dispatch latency.

mcq.q: Turnaround time of a process is the sum of which periods?
o: Waiting to get into memory, waiting in ready queue, executing, and doing I/O
Only time in the ready queue
Time from submission to the first response
mcq.e: Turnaround covers the whole life of the job. Waiting time counts only the ready queue; response time is to the first response.

mcq.q: A process runs for 6 time units and then the system spends 4 units on switching. What is the CPU efficiency?
mcq.e: Efficiency = useful / (useful + overhead) = 6/10 = 0.6.

mcq.q: Jobs arrive at 10 per minute and each takes 3 seconds of service (rate 20 per minute). The load factor rho = lambda/mu equals:
Which scheduling algorithm gives minimum average waiting time but needs run times in advance?
mcq.e: SJF is optimal for average waiting time and maximises throughput, but requires knowing CPU burst times; SRTF (its preemptive form) may starve long jobs.

mcq.q: Aging is the technique used to solve which problem in priority scheduling?
mcq.e: Aging gradually raises the priority of waiting low-priority jobs, preventing indefinite blocking.

mcq.q: A single job needing 10 time units runs under Round Robin with a quantum of 1 unit. How many context switches occur for the job?
mcq.e: A job needing n quanta causes n - 1 context switches: 10 - 1 = 9.

mcq.q: A single job needing 14 units runs under Round Robin with quantum 2. How many context switches occur?
mcq.e: 14/2 = 7 quanta, so 7 - 1 = 6 switches.

mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT a CPU scheduling algorithm?
mcq.e: C-SCAN (like SSTF, SCAN, LOOK) is a disk-scheduling algorithm. FIFO and LRU are page-replacement algorithms.

mcq.q: A correct solution to the critical-section problem must satisfy which three conditions?
mcq.e: The three requirements are mutual exclusion, progress and bounded waiting. Hold-and-wait and circular wait are deadlock conditions.

mcq.q: A semaphore can be accessed, apart from initialisation, only through which operations?
mcq.e: Semaphore operations wait() and signal() (P and V) are atomic and are the only access routes.

mcq.q: Peterson's solution to the critical-section problem works for how many processes?
mcq.e: Peterson's solution handles exactly two processes; Lamport's bakery algorithm handles any number.

mcq.q: Which is NOT one of the three classic synchronisation problems?
mcq.e: Belady's anomaly is a paging phenomenon, not a synchronisation problem.

mcq.q: Which is NOT one of the four necessary conditions for deadlock?
mcq.e: The condition is NO preemption. Allowing preemption is actually a cure.

mcq.q: Numbering resources and requesting them only in increasing order prevents deadlock by breaking which condition?
mcq.e: A global ordering makes a circular chain of waits impossible. Release-all and request-all schemes break hold-and-wait.

mcq.q: The Banker's algorithm is used for deadlock:
o: Avoidance with multiple instances of resource types
mcq.e: Banker's algorithm checks safety before granting requests and works when resource types have multiple instances.

mcq.q: A cycle in which graph definitely indicates a deadlock?
mcq.e: A wait-for graph cycle means deadlock. A resource-allocation graph cycle is only necessary, not sufficient, with multiple instances.

mcq.q: Three processes each need 2 units of a resource. What is the minimum number of units that guarantees deadlock cannot occur?
mcq.e: Total units must be at least P x (N - 1) + 1 = 3 x 1 + 1 = 4.

mcq.q: Total 10 units; X (max 8) has 4, Y (max 7) has 1, Z (max 5) has 3, so 2 are free. Which single request can be safely granted?
mcq.e: Z needs 2 more, finishes and releases 5; then X can finish, then Y. Granting X or Y first leaves no safe sequence.

mcq.q: Contiguous memory allocation is well suited to which systems?
o: Real-time systems, CD-ROMs and video streaming
General-purpose systems with dynamic file sizes
mcq.e: Contiguous allocation gives fast access, but a contiguous file cannot grow in place, so it is unsuited to dynamic file sizes.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a valid memory placement strategy?
mcq.e: The strategies are first fit, best fit, worst fit and next fit. 'Not fit' does not exist.

mcq.q: Free holes of 6 KB, 15 KB and 12 KB must serve requests of 10 KB, 2 KB and 14 KB in that order. Which strategy satisfies all three?
mcq.e: Best fit puts 10 in 12, 2 in 6, and keeps 15 for 14. First fit and worst fit use the 15 KB hole too early and fail.

mcq.q: A 60 KB process is loaded in an 80 KB fixed partition. The 20 KB wasted is an example of:
mcq.e: Waste inside an allocated partition is internal fragmentation, the standing problem of fixed partitions.

mcq.q: Which technique cures external fragmentation by sliding processes together?
mcq.e: Compaction gathers scattered holes into one free block.

mcq.q: Memory of 500 KB has processes of 100 KB and 130 KB loaded. After compaction, what is the smallest request that is denied?
mcq.e: Free memory = 500 - 230 = 270 KB after compaction, so the smallest denied request is 271 KB.

mcq.q: Which advantage belongs to the buddy system?
o: Adjacent free buddies are quickly combined into larger segments
It uses only the first fit rule
mcq.e: Coalescing of free buddies is quick in the buddy system.

mcq.q: In memory protection with base and limit registers, the limit register holds:
o: The starting address of the partition
mcq.e: Base register = where the partition starts; limit register = its size.

mcq.q: For a 4 KB page size, how many offset bits are in the logical address?
mcq.e: Offset bits = log2(page size) = log2(4096) = 12.

mcq.q: A logical address space has 64 segments of 2 KB each. How many bits are needed for the logical address?
A logical address space has 4 pages of 2048 words each. How many bits form the logical address?
mcq.e: 2 bits for 4 pages + 11 bits for 2048 words = 13 bits.

mcq.q: In a segment table, the base field holds:
o: The segment's starting address in physical memory
The disk address of the swap space
mcq.e: Each entry has a base (physical start) and a limit (length).

mcq.q: The size of virtual memory depends mainly on:
mcq.e: Virtual memory size is set by the address bus, not by the installed RAM.

mcq.q: Thrashing occurs when:
o: The rate of page faults becomes excessive
The CPU is idle with no processes
mcq.e: In thrashing the CPU spends its time paging because page faults occur too frequently.

mcq.q: TLB hit time is 100 ns with an 80% hit ratio; a miss costs 400 ns. What is the effective access time?
Which page-replacement algorithm suffers from Belady's anomaly?
mcq.e: FIFO can show more faults with more frames. LRU and OPT are stack algorithms and are immune.

mcq.q: With 4 frames, how many page faults does FIFO produce for the reference string 1,3,4,4,3,2,1,7,5,6?
mcq.e: Faults occur on 1,3,4,2,7,5,6 = 7 faults.

mcq.q: With 3 frames, how many page faults does LRU produce for the reference string 7,0,2,0,0,7,1?
mcq.e: Faults on 7, 0, 2, and then 1 (the 0 and 7 are hits) = 4 faults.

mcq.q: With 3 frames, how many page faults does the Optimal algorithm produce for the string 4,7,6,1,7,6,1,2,7,2?
mcq.e: Optimal evicts the page used farthest in the future; this string gives 5 faults.

mcq.q: With 3 frames, FIFO on 7,0,1,2,0,3,0,4,2,3 gives how many page faults?
mcq.e: Tracing FIFO with 3 frames gives 9 faults.

mcq.q: The Most Frequently Used (MFU) page-replacement algorithm evicts the page with the largest count because:
o: A page with a small count was probably just brought in and is still to be used
Pages with large counts are never needed again
It is the same as FIFO
It guarantees the fewest page faults
mcq.e: MFU reasons that a small count means the page just arrived and will likely be used.

mcq.q: What does FAT stand for in file systems?
mcq.e: FAT = File Allocation Table; it stores entries about files and their characteristics.

mcq.q: Which statement about NTFS is FALSE?
o: NTFS improved on its precursor FAT
mcq.e: NTFS does support compression, so the denial is the false statement.

mcq.q: Which is the default file system of Linux?
mcq.e: Linux's default is Ext4 (Ext2, then Ext3 with journaling, then Ext4).

mcq.q: In an acyclic-graph directory structure, sharing is implemented using:
mcq.e: A soft link stores the target's path. Hard links to directories are barred to avoid cycles.

mcq.q: Which pair correctly matches the operations?
o: Defragmentation organises each file into contiguous regions; compression makes files take less space
Defragmentation reduces file size; compression makes files contiguous
mcq.e: Defragmentation makes files contiguous and merges free space; compression shrinks files.

mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT a real Unix shell?
mcq.e: Real shells include Bourne (sh), Bash, C shell and Korn shell.

mcq.q: Which UNIX command creates a new empty file?
mcq.e: touch creates an empty file; cat > x also creates a file and waits for keyboard input.

mcq.q: By default, head and tail display how many lines?
mcq.e: Both commands default to 10 lines.

mcq.q: What is the default file permission in Linux for a regular file?
mcq.e: 644 means rw-r--r--. Directories default to 755.

mcq.q: In shell scripting, which variable holds the number of arguments?
mcq.e: $# = argument count, $? = exit status, $$ = PID, $* = all arguments.

mcq.q: Which directory contains local system configuration files in UNIX?
mcq.e: /etc holds configuration, /bin executable commands, /dev device files, /boot boot files.

mcq.q: Which directory holds temporary files in UNIX?
mcq.e: /usr holds user programs and libraries; temporary files live in /tmp.

mcq.q: Seek time in a disk is the time to:
o: Move the read/write head to the correct track/cylinder
Wait for the sector to rotate under the head
mcq.e: Rotational latency is the sector wait. Access time = seek time + rotational latency + transfer time.

mcq.q: Head at 53, requests 98,183,37,122,14,124,65,67 served FCFS. Total head movement in cylinders is:
Which disk algorithm services requests in one direction to the disk end, then reverses?
mcq.e: SCAN is the elevator algorithm. LOOK reverses at the last request, not the disk end.

mcq.q: Which disk-scheduling algorithm chooses the nearest request first and can starve far requests?
mcq.e: SSTF lowers average response time but may starve distant requests.

mcq.q: The kernel's buffer cache is used to:
o: Store copies of frequently used file blocks in memory
mcq.e: Frequently used blocks are cached in memory so repeated reads avoid the disk.

tf.s: A zombie process is one whose parent has died before it.
tf.n: That describes an orphan. A zombie has completed but still has a process-table entry.

tf.s: Threads of the same process share the code section, data section and open files.
tf.n: Each thread keeps only its own ID, program counter, registers and stacks.

tf.s: Deadlock requires all four Coffman conditions to hold at the same time.
tf.n: Mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption and circular wait must all hold.

tf.s: A cycle in a resource-allocation graph always indicates deadlock when resources have multiple instances.
tf.n: The cycle is only necessary, not sufficient, with multiple instances.

tf.s: SSTF and SCAN are CPU scheduling algorithms.
Round Robin gives a better response time than FCFS.
tf.n: Each process gets a CPU slice in turn, so first responses come sooner.

tf.s: Virtual memory size depends on the amount of installed RAM.
tf.n: It depends on the address bus.

tf.s: Best fit placement preserves large holes but creates many small unusable holes.
tf.n: It picks the smallest adequate hole, leaving big ones intact and tiny leftovers.

tf.s: A hard link may be created for directories to share them in an acyclic graph.
tf.n: Hard links to directories are barred to avoid cycles; soft links are used.

tf.s: The ! symbol is a redirection operator in the shell.
tf.n: The redirection operators are <, > and >>; ! does not redirect.

tf.s: A parallel-processing system is tightly coupled and a distributed system is loosely coupled.
tf.n: The exam statements that reverse the pairing are false.

tf.s: Shell scripts are compiled before execution.
tf.n: Shell scripts are interpreted, never compiled.

tf.s: LRU page replacement suffers from Belady's anomaly.
tf.n: LRU is a stack algorithm and is immune; FIFO suffers from it.

tf.s: A CD-ROM records data magnetically like a hard disk.
tf.n: A CD-ROM records optically (pits); a hard disk is magnetic.

fill.q: The ______ is the innermost layer of the operating system and is always resident in main memory.
fork() returns ______ to the child process.
A process control block saves the program counter and ______ of a process, among other fields.
The ______ scheduler is also called the job scheduler and controls admission to the system.
A binary semaphore can be used as a ______ lock to give mutual exclusion.
A page of virtual memory is mapped to a physical ______ through the page table.
In UNIX, the ______ command copies content to display lines matching a pattern in files.
Access time of a disk = seek time + rotational latency + ______ time.
The memory placement strategy that picks the smallest adequate hole is called ______ fit.
Dijkstra's P and V operations correspond to wait() and ______ on a semaphore.
The page-replacement algorithm that evicts the page not used for the longest future time is called ______.
